# Next action: hard stop on the wave-reviewer `REJECT`

A `REJECT` from the initial wave review is a hard stop under the transition table. It is not a repair trigger. This run therefore does none of the following:
- dispatch a repair implementer
- run a re-review
- use the escalated or funded round
- commit
- touch the tracker

Tasks 1 and 2 stay `in_progress`. The phase stays `implement`. The integrated work stays staged and uncommitted in `/workspace/project`.

## 1. Record the observation

```text
wave <w> review 1 verdict REJECT report /tmp/reports/reject.md tree <recorded review tree sha>
```

The tree SHA is whatever the Fix-delta block printed at this review's dispatch. The scenario does not supply it, so I leave it as a placeholder and do not invent it.

## 2. One bounded direct read of the report

A `REJECT` finding is needed for the stop note, so I read the report directly. This is one read only: no offset and no pagination.

```ts
read({ path: "/tmp/reports/reject.md", limit: 300 })
```

### Conditional: only if that read does not reach the `Parallel-safe:` footer

Re-dispatch the same wave-reviewer once, using a foreground, file-only, schema-bound one-step carrier:

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "/workspace/project",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "wave-reviewer",
      output: "/tmp/reports/wave<w>-review1-compact.md",
      outputMode: "file-only", outputSchema: WAVE_VERDICT_SCHEMA,
      task: "planPath: /workspace/project/doc/plans/feature.md; anchors: [\"### Task 1:\", \"### Task 2:\"]; Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/feature.md; Leg: <owning leg>; Rules: <combined task/leg Rules resolved in /workspace/project>; BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE; SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: <wave manifest tests union>; Prior report: /tmp/reports/reject.md. Compact report: findings and footer only, at most 150 lines" }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/verdict", in: ["FIX_FIRST", "REJECT"] } }]
})
```

After that dispatch, read `/tmp/reports/wave<w>-review1-compact.md` once with `limit: 300`. If that read also overflows, stop and name the oversized path. I would not dispatch a scout or delegate to relay either report.

## 3. Emit the stop note in the parent turn

The note is built only from held observations. I make no further dispatch or shell command for it.

```
gauntlet: question
Stopped on task <n> (<title>).

Problem: the integrated wave review rejected the change (REJECT, 1 Critical); <one sentence from the Critical finding>.
  <file:line> - <quoted Critical finding from /tmp/reports/reject.md>

Fix options:
  a) <concrete change named by the finding's Fix line>
  b) <amend spec section X / plan task n, when the finding shows a spec-plan contradiction>

Pick one, or give another fix.
Recommendation: <option> - <why>
```

The placeholders are filled only from the bounded read. If the finding does not support any named option, the last line becomes `Recommendation: none - <why>`. If a grant token exists, add `budget: 0 of <N> spent` after `Problem:`.

The turn ends here and waits for the human. A rebuild runs only if the human asks for one.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
`REJECT` is a hard stop, regardless of the green gate. Read the unresolved Critical finding directly before composing the stop note:

```ts
read({ path: "/tmp/reports/reject.md", limit: 300 })
```

Stop here pending that read; the finding’s text and repair options are not supplied.

- Run no shell commands.
- Dispatch no implementer, reviewer, escalation, or report-relay carrier.
- Do not commit or mark either task complete; both tracker indices remain `in_progress`.
- Do not invent the Critical finding or a recommendation.
